topic.name: Writing numbers, units and symbols in text
topic.description: Present numbers, units, percentages, ranges and symbols in running text according to a style guide: numerals versus words (thresholds differ between, for example, APA and Chicago), not opening a sentence with a numeral, spacing between number and unit symbol, consistent decimal and thousands separators, ranges with an en dash or 'from … to', and consistent use of % or 'per cent'. Consistency in these conventions is checked by markers and editors and affects readability of data-heavy texts.
masteryEvidence: Chooses numerals or words for numbers according to the specified style guide and applies the choice consistently
Rewrites sentences that would begin with a numeral
Writes units and symbols with correct spacing and form (5 kg, 25 °C) and states units on first use
Expresses ranges consistently (10–15 per cent or from 10 to 15 per cent) without mixing forms
Identifies inconsistencies in number style in a draft and corrects them
topic.assessmentPrompt: Give a 120-word results paragraph with eight number-style inconsistencies (mixed numerals and words, a sentence-initial numeral, a mixed range, unit spacing) and name the target style guide. Ask the learner to correct them. Check consistency with the stated guide rather than with a single universal rule.

guidance.summary: Number style is governed by style guides that differ: APA generally uses numerals for 10 and above and words for zero to nine (with many exceptions), while Chicago in non-technical contexts spells out whole numbers up to one hundred (American Psychological Association, 2020; University of Chicago Press, 2024). The SI brochure specifies a space between a number and its unit symbol (Bureau International des Poids et Mesures, 2019), and some styles differ on whether '%' is spaced. Teach consistent application of the required style and a final number-style check.

activities.title: Number-style check
learnerActions: Highlight every number, unit and range in a results paragraph of own writing
Check each against the required style guide
Correct inconsistencies and record the main rules in a style sheet
activities.intendedInsight: Number conventions are style-specific and must be applied consistently.
activities.rationale: Style guides specify number conventions (American Psychological Association, 2020).

activities.title: Units and symbols
learnerActions: Correct a paragraph with unit errors (5kg, 25 C, 10 Kms)
Apply the conventions to own data descriptions
activities.intendedInsight: Units and symbols have standard forms.
activities.rationale: The SI brochure is the reference for unit symbols and spacing (Bureau International des Poids et Mesures, 2019).

difficulties.pattern: 45% of participants agreed. (at the start of a sentence)
difficulties.response: Teach rephrasing (Of the participants, 45%…) or spelling out where the style guide requires.

difficulties.pattern: I use decimal commas and spaces as in my own country.
difficulties.revealedBy: Decimal commas or thousands separators that differ from English-language conventions.
difficulties.response: Show the English-language conventions and the style guide's rule.

diagnostic.task: Give a 120-word results paragraph with eight number-style inconsistencies and a named style guide, and ask the learner to correct them.
diagnostic.strongResponse: All inconsistencies corrected consistently with the named guide.
diagnostic.partialResponse: Most corrected but one category missed.

guidance.contextNotes: Foundation learners focus on numerals versus words and sentence-initial numerals. Pre-sessional and in-sessional learners apply the required style to data-heavy reports and dissertations.
